faces.f:
"The emergence of the Eldrazi isn't necessarily a bad thing, as long as you've already lived a fulfilling and complete life without regrets."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
The barest taste of Eldrazi power shatters both realms and identities.
The Eldrazi hunger without limit and consume without pause.

"The brood spread far faster than we could kill it. I fear the worst is yet to come."
—*The War Diaries*

"Whatever the Eldrazi's purpose is, it has nothing to do with something so insignificant as us."
—Nirthu, lone missionary
Gremlins in the wild feed on nodules of pure aether, which are also prized by miners.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."

"To survive up here, I've learned when to use my harpoon and when to just enjoy the view."
—Kadhu, skywhaler
The wills of mortals shift as the tide ebbs and flows.
"Citizens, do not resist. This is for your safety. Tezzeret bids you to surrender your inventions. Now."
Another imminent battle subsided in busy snuffling and carefree rooting.

"Within our minds are limitless depths. Dive down, but don't forget to surface."
—Teferi

"Once I supply the breeze, you'll see your warriors for the smoke they truly are."
—Alexi, zephyr mage
Ugin saw the gem that connected Bolas to his Meditation Realm as the key to his brother's downfall.

"The union of sea and sky makes a perfect cover."
—Talrand, sky summoner
Creators live for that moment of inspiration: precious, profound, perfect.
Only one vault was great enough to hold Emrakul.
Some spellcrafting mistakes go on to become spells of their own.

"The cost of your opposition will be extracted from your wits."
—Nekusar, the Mindrazer
"Let's start fresh, shall we?"
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.

"You speak to me of the threat of Ulamog. But do not forget: they came as three."
—Ugin, to Jace Beleren
Malice spreads on wings of tyranny.
"Why throw away a perfectly good identity?"
The light sigh of its breath whistles through its bones.
No part goes to waste.
Ulamog's tentacles, their touch like burning ice, rummaged through his soul and stung his memories one by one.
When tempers run high, it's easy to lose your head.

"Molten earth has no anger of its own. Only by infusing it with your own rage can the magma seethe and take shape."
—Koth of the Hammer
In the moment before her execution, she realized what it meant to be a pyromancer, to be alive, to be Chandra.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
"You burn. I'll pillage."
"Catch me if you can."
It fears no sword and leaves no bones behind.
The ground erupted in time with the hedron's thrum, a dirge of the last days.

"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them."
—Euphemia, Nexus watcher

"'I have arrived,' bellowed Brawn, and the plane shuddered."
—*Scroll of Beginnings*

"Vine-wreathed, he nurtures life among the dead."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Emrakul does not grant wishes. Desires simply align to her will.

"Animals commune with their environment without the need for language. Theirs is a fundamental connection that surpasses flimsy words."
—Vivien Reid
With the Hekma breached and its protection removed, the deserts swept in.
He protects the fetid bog from light, life, and the hideous sound of laughter.

"Ach! Hans, run! It's the lhurgoyf!"
—Saffi Eriksdotter, last words

"What would Urza think, I wonder, if he could hear how the nature mages still snarl at his name, but venerate the work of his apprentice?"
—Teferi, to Jhoira
The greatest wonders of nature are found in the smallest saplings straining toward the canopy.

"Bright as any dinosaur—and just as with other great hunters, its colors are a warning."
—Huatli

"When the land is angry, so are they."
—Nissa Revane
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
"This world was once so much more than the confines of Naktamun."
"The curse is broken."
He'd chosen a sunlit clearing with open skies and an ample brook. All that remained was to find a worthy sapling.
The first satyr to wake after a revel must search for the site of the next one.

"Survival rule 782: There are *always* more scute bugs."
—Zurdi, goblin shortcutter

"As long as there is a single shred of life, there is hope."
—Nissa Revane

"All who set foot in Paliano are pawns in someone's play for power."
—Marchesa, the Black Rose
"At first, the equations were simply numbers. But in those numbers I saw a story, and in that story I saw a pattern, and suddenly it all fit together!"
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.
Cyclical and spiral patterns are the specialty of the Gyre Clade, which seeks to revitalize the cycles of nature.
Havoc is a small price to pay for data.
During the collision of the shards, entire ways of life disappeared without a trace.
As the great scourge passed by, Zendikar shivered, then lay silent.
"Yavimaya is one being—one vastness of rippling leaves, one deepness of roots, and one chatter of animals—of which I am one part."

"I've seen death before. My mother succumbing to illness, my comrades bleeding on the battlefield . . . But I'd never seen anything as dreadful as that."
—Taani, berserker of Etlan
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.
The first tentative flaps are like a song to his soul.

"What dies grows the [illegible]"
—Clawed-out statue inscription
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
Forged by divine hands to wander mortal realms.
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.
Progress leads to inspiration.
Only the Eldrazi mind thinks in the warped paths required to open the hedrons and tap the power within.

"Gods don't die. They merely slumber."
—Ayli, Kamsa cleric

"I use maps to find out where explorers have already been. Then I go the other way."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter

"We shall forever roam."
—Ayli, high priest of the Eternal Pilgrims
Despite the magic that sustains Gonti's life, the crime lord is often described as heartless.

"You've begun to understand the hedrons' true purpose," said Ugin. "The Eldrazi can be imprisoned."
"And how did that work out last time?" asked Jace.
"Arise, great one, and cleanse the world of our enemies!"
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
Most mirrors show your reflection. Others show your potential.
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.

"The sun banishes darkness every morning. I too will rise with such assuredness."
—Huatli

"Good ideas don't take time. They take a lot of bad ideas first."
—Ral Zarek

"The pain of exploring is less than the pain of not knowing."
—Tamiyo

"The continual rise of the downtrodden is as inevitable as vines usurping a forest."
—Vraska
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Left barren by the Brothers' War, it stands as a stark reminder of Dominaria's likely fate should the Coalition fail.
It powers the dreams of Ghirapur.

"As Terisiare's mines ran dry, scrap metal became increasingly plentiful."
—*The Antiquities War*
There is a sanctuary that reveals itself only to those graced by the *eludha*—the mystical connection between bonder and monster.

"Urza fortified every thirty miles on the path to Tomakul, creating a network of trenches the brothers would trade for decades."
—*The Antiquities War*

"The rushing water is as the God-Pharaoh. It encompasses all. It nurtures all."
—Temmet, vizier of Naktamun
Without Vantress's knowledge, the realm would lose itself in darkness.
After years of silence, the caves once again echo with the grisly sounds of Phyrexians preparing for war.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.

"He watches from above. He watches from below. He watches from within."
—Inscription on Tel-Jilad, the Tree of Tales
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.

"Look, and see the future."
—Ayli, high priest of the Eternal Pilgrims
Soothing whispers invite travelers to step closer, closer, closer . . . until they vanish soundlessly beneath the surface.
Each temple is a door to a horrible future.

"The wilds are unpredictable. Rivers change course, trees shuffle and bend, rocks split and scurry. But mark my words, traveler—the main thing that'll change out there is *you*."
—Sturwynn, Boundary Lands ranger

"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them."
—Pulan, Bant orchardist
At full moon, the river seeps over its banks and crawls through the woods like a blanket of serpents.
A smoldering storm of chilling fire.
A seething locus of reverent rage.
What once spied upon Mirrodin from above now waits below for another to assume control.
Between jagged, snowcapped peaks, the dense bands of hardy evergreens provide the perfect cover for roving bands of orc and goblin raiders.
When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.

"The sylex blast marked not only the end of the war, but the end of Dominaria as most knew it."
—*The Antiquities War*

"Finally, a stroke of luck! Had to taste the water myself to believe it wasn't a mirage."
—Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
Lush growth spreads like a ferocious blaze across the Otarian hillsides.
The gate of every kithkin doun is a cunning trap, intended to spill visitors into an oubliette from which there is no escape.
When asked how many paths reach enlightenment, the monk kicked a heap of sand. "Count," he smiled, "and then find more grains."
Still to the ignorant eye, yet bursting with life. A million actions and reactions, unstoppable as the dawn.
A haunted fog known as the Nebelgast shrouds the cities along Nephalia's coast.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
Mage-students who see beauty in patterns and equations choose Quandrix, the college of numeromancy.
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
Along the outer girders, in gold filigree, are inscribed the names of all those who fell to their deaths during construction.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
Gnolls make offerings to sinister forces in the shadow-drenched chasms.
The boiling seas around Shiv provided a welcome layer of protection for the reclaimed Mana Rig.
The gods known to the merfolk as Ula, Emeria, and Cosi were nothing more than false memories of a monstrous trinity: the Eldrazi titans Ulamog, Emrakul, and Kozilek.
Enter and comprehend the perfection of orchestrated life.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
Young Eldrazi crawl forth from the dust, compelled by a greater will.
Everything is flammable in the Burning Isles, even the mana itself.

"We move because the earth does."
—Bruse Tarl, Goma Fada nomad

"The Phyrexian's monuments of today will be nothing but dust tomorrow. With enough tomorrows, so will their rule."
—Koth
Amid rumors of war, the third act of *The Absolution of the Guildpact* was quickly rewritten as a tragedy.
Deep in Eldraine's wilds, strange eyelike appendages twined among the vines and faerie lights.

"The voice calls me here, yet I see only bones. Is this more dragon trickery?"
—Sarkhan Vol

"The war polluted the land, turning what had once been fruitful fields into fetid morasses of mud and rusted corpses."
—*The Antiquities War*
In his hunger for power and knowledge, Urza dug deep into Dominaria's ancient past.
Urza threw himself into his research, pushing the boundaries of both possibility and morality.
Urza studied the creations of the Thran not simply to learn from them, but to surpass them.
It is everywhere you've ever been.
A verdant paradox of primal logic.
Life and death mixing together, both ends of the same cycle giving rise to something else.

"Multani's heart is a seed, and all of Yavimaya is its flower. There is as much life here as in the rest of Dominaria together."
—Karn
As magnigoth trees expanded across the sea into Almaaz and New Argive, it became clear Yavimaya's borders were never confined by its coastline.
"Control the Great Conduit? You might as well try to divert a river with your hands."

faces.f: It was a time for rebuilding, but first Ikoria's wrecked cities had to be cleared of monsters.
Survivors put the strength of former war mounts to good use clearing the rubble of Orazca.
With their ancient enemy vanquished, the angels of New Capenna turned their eyes to their former captors: demons.
Phyrexia was defeated, but the repercussions of the invasion rippled through the Blind Eternities.
The glistening oil had been rendered inert, but planes wouldn't begin to truly heal until every last drop was purged.
For those who survived, being prepared for the next crisis became one of the greatest virtues.
After the invasion, many wanted to leave a life of violence. But once you're a Reckoner, you die a Reckoner.
Conflict is a constant. Only the enemies change.
The relic shattered, and something in Nahiri broke as well.
The creature was unlike any Nissa had seen, but she dealt with it as she would any threat.
When Nissa tapped into Zhalfir's leylines, she was shocked to feel not a piece of Dominaria, but a plane all its own.
Light shone on parts of the undercity for the first time in centuries.
Reconstructing the past is Lorehold's specialty.

"When all the stories find their ends, a new one shall begin."
—*The Endsaga*
Danitha had spent her whole life preparing to lead House Capashen, but she mourned that the opportunity had come so soon.
To hear them tell it, they charged bare-handed into New Phyrexia and beat up Elesh Norn all by themselves.
Worlds apart, Huatli built a device Saheeli would have been proud of.
"Our strength lies not in our walls, but in our people."
"Zendikar is *my* home!"
They called her unique insight a "gift." Then she saw the truth, and suddenly it was a "threat."
The story circle continues.
Stranded on New Capenna without a spark, he faced five families out for blood.
Renegade turned revolutionary turned rebuilder.
The Phyrexian design had to go, but the materials could be put to good use.
"Try to keep up, Djeru. We have lots of work to do."
"Today, we become gods again."
Like Orn before it, Drannith was reduced to a playground for Ikoria's monsters.
The glistening oil had been rendered inert, but planes wouldn't begin to truly heal until every last drop was purged.

—*The Endsaga*

To hear them tell it, they charged bare-handed into New Phyrexia and beat up Elesh Norn all by themselves.

"Zendikar is *my* home!"
They called her unique insight a "gift." Then she saw the truth, and suddenly it was a "threat."
The story circle continues.
The Phyrexian design had to go, but the materials could be put to good use.
"Today, we become gods again."
First-years quickly learn how the Vastlands earned its name.

"Archons dispense justice according to an ancient, and flawed, premise."
—Nissa Revane
"Honorable tactics are for honorable foes. These werewolves are preying on innocent travelers. I'll stab them in the back while they sleep if I have to."
Avacyn's holy warriors kept hope alive in her darkest hours. Now they will carry that hope across Innistrad.
Some protection requires a bit of finesse.

"They have forsaken their vows. The edict of the Circle demands their voices be silenced."
—Syr Tasdale, knight of Ardenvale
"The noble work of our order is to infuse all life on Esper with etherium. Our goal will be reached more rapidly if new life is . . . suppressed."
No more shall the righteous cower before evil.
Her resentment vanished as strange, unknown lands opened up before her.
Right before his demise, he experienced a shattering revelation.
Students at the Dekatia Academy learn that being sent to study with her is a lesson in itself.
The relic's purpose? Its design? Whatever the intent, it is now a mere curiosity that breaks up the horizon.
Ivold gasped in surprise. Either a very strange insect had crawled onto one of the lenses or he was seeing geists at last!

"Isn't she the cutest thing you've almost seen?"
—Doen, purveyor of exotic pets

"My flesh holds no secrets, monster. The spirit of Mirrodin will fight on."
—Vy Covalt, Mirran resistance

"Your first mistake was thinking I would let you live long enough to make a second."
—Sarnvax, Gitaxian sective
"Poor, lost mage. Your feet are on land, yet you're in over your head, aren't you?"
The results of Rashmi's experimentation forced her to consider the possibility that multitudinous realities existed beyond her own.
Tomorrow belongs to those who prepare for it today.

"There's a hole in your plan."
—Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.
What nature makes, magic can modify.

"The blood of the weak shall be the ink with which we scribe great Yawgmoth's glorious name."
—Stronghold architect, journal
"Beautiful, isn't it?" crowed Crovax. "They fought together. Now they will die together."
The line between dream and death is gauzy and fragile. She leads those too near it from one side to the other.
Fear is as effective a weapon as the blade.
Where treachery and oblivion converge.
Liliana developed a fondness for the moment when roaring becomes squealing.
"Shame to let good gold go to the grave."
Wreckage from the Phyrexian Invasion provided the rats with a seemingly unlimited number of breeding grounds.
No part goes to waste.
The lamps on Wyndmoor Street snuff themselves at midnight and refuse to relight, afraid to illuminate what lies in the darkness.
Elspeth feared that her trespass into Nyx would not go unanswered.
If there's anything a werewolf hates, it's a collar—especially Avacyn's Collar, the symbol of her church.
"I've been all over this world. I even remember some of those places."
Deep beneath the ice, beneath the soil and the rock, Dominaria's fire still burned hot.

"It's rarely worth questioning where the mana comes from. Just be grateful."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage
"The devils use fire. Why shouldn't we?"

"If you had just one wish, what would it be? Gold, or angel song? Finding a lost love, or finding your way back home? Let me sing a song about one wish that came true . . ."
—Ellywick Tumblestrum

"He steals power from treasure after treasure, and what does it do for the ouphe? Nothing."
—Jhoira
If you feel the ground quake, run. If you hear its bellow, flee. If you see its teeth, it's too late.

"We are never without guidance, if we but seek it."
—Taaveti of Kelsinko, elvish hunter

"On this plane, the use of magic can provoke a ferocious reprisal from nature. Whoever the Eldrazi were, their relics left Zendikar forever enraged."
—Jace Beleren

"Dead or alive, my creations are stronger than Jin-Gitaxias's septic minions."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger
There were no tombstones in orochi territory. Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.

The hippo grows wings to fight the condor.
—Nantuko teaching
The Izzet quickly suspended their policy of lifetime guarantees.
Prismari students dance in the tension between passion and perfection.
Accept one favor from an ouphe, and you're doomed to accept another.
"I told Jace that Ravnica would fall apart if he didn't take his responsibilities seriously. I didn't want to be right."
No one has properly answered her favorite riddle: "Why should I spare your life?"

"Etherium is limited. Innovation is not."
—Tezzeret
The embodiment of yearning, forever drifting the deserts to find what had once made it whole.

"Arcum is a babbling fool! Phyrexian technology is our greatest blessing. Take this delightful trinket for instance . . ."
—Heidar, Rimewind master
Infinite possibilities contained in a finite space.
It harnesses the power of night in a land where daylight fears to show itself.
The eastern passage into the city is filled with reminders that the patriars are literally looking down on you.
Deep within the Cabal's vault, the Mirari pulsed like a dead sun—and its darkness radiated across Otaria.
Panopticon, forge of the Darksteel Eye, home of Mirrodin's keeper.
Where wasted life cries out to be reborn.
When the aven scouts located the tower in Esper, the Knights of the Reliquary set off on a righteous crusade to recover their lost treasures.
Amid rumors of war, the third act of *The Absolution of the Guildpact* was quickly rewritten as a tragedy.

faces.f:
"The land promises nothing and keeps its promise."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"My past holds only pain and loss. I will conquer it by creating the perfect future."
—Ixidor, reality sculptor
"I don't need a map to find riches."

Keep a green tree in your heart and perhaps the singing bird will come.
—Chinese proverb
Be it ever so crumbled, there's no place like home.
At his behest the Kami War began to regain That Which Was Taken.
They're even more dangerous outside the arena.
The most powerful among them, Ashuza rules Veluk with flame and claw.

"There is no place for mercy in defense of our lives."
—Ta-Spon, Cho-Arrim executioner
She provides marks of protection to those she chooses as family.
The Kor forsake roots for the winding of the path; forsake voices for the silence of the mind; forsake all else for the poverty of isolation.
The justice of dragons demands more than just an eye for an eye.

"Just think of me as the storm before the calm."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
The smallest seed of regret can bloom into redemption.

"A ruler wears a crown while the rest of us wear hats, but which would you rather have when it's raining?"
—Barrin, *Principia*

"I see more than others do because I know where to look."
—Saprazzan vizier

"Your attack has been rendered harmless. It is, however, quite pretty."
—Saprazzan vizier
He wished for knowledge, but not for the will to apply it.
Karn said nothing—he just grasped the powerstone and squeezed tightly. The wild flashing ceased.

Seek balance in all things—as long as the scales are weighted in your favor.
—Vodalian saying

"Remove their power, and their will to fight will follow."
—Tolarian wizard
Lat-Nam wizards trade knowledge on scrolls made of magic so they can better guard against thieves and spies.

"Life is a maze. This is one of its dead ends."
—Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
Those who expect betrayal at every turn are seldom disappointed.
At the academy, "show and tell" too often becomes "run and hide."
"Take your time."

"If I wanted your opinion, I'd have told you what it was."
—Pemmin, Riptide survivor
Doing something at the last minute isn't so bad when you can make that minute last.
"What separates us from mere beasts is the capacity for self-improvement."
The Patriarch is long dead, but his name still stains the lips of cultists.

"Eye of twilight, give us sight.
Take our offer, give us might.
Make our power tears of night."
The shadow of the candle looms tall even as its light grows dim.
Abandon hope . . . .
Even the putrid muscles of the dead can provide strength to those loathsome enough to consume them.
Knives in the sky, cries in the air, and blood on the ground.
"The bigger they are, the faster they rot."
He controlled the zombies even before his own death; now nothing can make them betray him.
"Power-hungry eunuchs, the curse of the dynasty, have thrown the masses of the people into the depths of misery."
A reward is worthless if you aren't around to enjoy it.
To be king, Numsgil did in Blog, who did in Unkful, who did in Viddle, who did in Loll, who did in Alrok . . . .
At the first sign of enemy scouts, Jula grinned and strapped on his diplomacy helmet.
"Next!"

"We have built a wall upon sand. The wall will vanish. The sand will remain."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
Many can stand where one would fall.

"To examine the causes of life, we must first have recourse to death."
—Mary Shelley, *Frankenstein*
Hanna was astounded. Mirri read every leaf and wisp of breeze like a book of ancient lore.

"We shun them not for their dream but for their refusal to let such a noble dream die a noble death."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

"I expected a fight, but I didn't expect it from the building itself."
—Gerrard
All the junk, refuse, and offal of the Krark Clan is diligently collected, melted down, and made into more junk, refuse, and offal.
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
"Hard to imagine," mused Hanna, stroking the petal, "such a lovely flower inspiring such greed."
The bigger they are, the stronger its pull.
As he repaired the ship's planeswalking engine, Karn saw for the first time how he could catalyze the *Weatherlight*'s evolution.
Elves believe the hydra-god Progenitus sleeps beneath Naya, feeding on forgotten magics.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.

Time passes, time crawls;
Time doesn't move at all.
The dark opening seemed to breathe the cold, damp air of the dead earth in a steady rhythm.

"Phyrexia is certainly dangerous, but I have to admire some of its innovations."
—Tezzeret
Rishada is the gateway to free trade—but the key will cost you.
Like the city, weakest at its foundation.
Among wizards, poor timing is the most consistent mistake.
The smartest—and only—goblin cabin boy aboard the *Weatherlight*, Squee has learned that intelligence and common sense are very different things. This matters little, however, since he has neither.
Sisay continued the quest for the Legacy even when Gerrard chose to abandon it. She is devoted to the cause of good at whatever the price.
The heir to the Legacy has finally returned to the *Weatherlight*.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.
Does it reflect the future that once was or the past that can never be?

"You."
—Sorin Markov

faces.f: "Only through sacred infection can a vessel become pure."
Tales of heroics fill the air between matches at Valor's Reach.
"People often miss the little details. Thankfully, every tiny mistake they make is a big clue for me!"
She wraps the fry nursery in nullwater so the ruckus of wayward mages doesn't bother the little ones.
"Turn your studies into uncompromising power. Only then will you be a royal mage."
No beast in Terisiare is more frightening than the man who haunts its woods.
Ever seeking a voice all its own.
"No risk, no reward!"
All her shows have a captive audience.
Thicker than thieves.
"The land lives and breathes, as we do. Nurture it, and it will respond in kind."
"Blor's defenses are still impervious!"

"The Third Advent brings hunger. Feed it, but never sate it. Hunger begets growth."
—*Path of the Pentarch*
An unnatural ruler for the natural world.
One squirrel in Krosa never goes hungry.
The throne was his in appearance only.
"Returned from your hunt? I hope you've brought me something good for my birthday."
"Definitely try this at home, kids!"
He requires no destination, just a direction—a welcome respite for the weary traveler upon the sea floor.
"Phyrexia has much to answer for."
He who bears the cap laughs last.
Niv-Mizzet enthusiastically rejected their bid to become an eleventh guild.
When it awoke, the five stirred from their slumber.
In Lim-Dûl's stead may he forever reign.
It doesn't hunt. It doesn't hunger. It simply waits as all oozes eventually find their way back to it.
Created to keep the library well-stocked.
She had been the first to call the city home. Many more would follow and find its sanctuary.
"xe [being organic pl 2:4] 'št[mother pl 2:2] [weep 2:3], loxuφ [being mixed organic/inorganic pl 2:4] φl[phyrexia-eternal-love] [comfort 1:2]. ^'elš norn.
The tag on its toe read "deceased." It vehemently disagreed.
"You'll eat it and you'll like it! Anyone care to argue?"

"All this nonsense made by mages
Rusts and crumbles through the ages."
—Aline Corralurn, "Inheritance"
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.

"What do you have that I cannot obtain?"
—Mairsil, the Pretender

"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?"
—Jhoira, master artificer

"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared."
—Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
Infinite possibilities contained in a finite space.

"When you can't find your way home, find home where you can."
—Rho, veteran hero

faces.f: "I fight for the suns, the surface, and everything in between."
"We lost our homes and our kin. We won't let those rotters take our future as well."

"Unworthy of consecration."
—Axsh, lesser cenobite

"Fall to your knees and welcome our embrace."
—Qal-Sha, Priest of Norn

"The Phyrexians *are* vulnerable. Do not despair. We will prevail!"
—Juryan, rebel leader
"We will mourn when there is time. For now, we survive."

"Rid them of their unfaithful organs. Bring new hearts to the unbelievers."
—*Tome of Machines*, verse 1703
The squabble over succession was quickly replaced by the struggle to survive.
"The infection has spread farther than we could glimpse from the heights of Taj-Nar."
"This war is not about loxodon or leonin, Sylvok or Auriok. To defeat these rotters, we must do it together."
The need to obey was inscribed on every plate in their bodies.
A symbol of what Mirrodin once was and hope for what it will be again.
As long as one drop of the oil exists, the joyous work continues.

"May our blessings sever the tongues of the forsaken."
—Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
A new bird of prey—one that hunts sentience.
The corruption stirred the heavens above, awaking a shining champion.
After the Battle of Liet Field, the white sun crested above Taj-Nar, bringing hope to all who survived the carnage.

"The Origin Query will wait. We must ensure we survive to return to it."
—Pelyus, vedalken ordinar
Blessed by the hands of Jin-Gitaxias.
Karn's creation is now his master.

"If left in the enemy's shape too long, it might be lost to them."
—Vy Covalt, Neurok agent

"The fleeting shadows of his primitive self have all but vanished."
—Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur
"Your ideas will be discarded and your will repurposed."
Accurate information is a precious commodity in times of war.

"They can't even comprehend nature. How could they improve it?"
—Venser
"There's no more time for secluded study. Answers are there only for those with the courage to take them."

"In its gaze I saw no mercy, no recognition that I was worthy to exist."
—Kara Vrist, Neurok agent

"Phyrexians are tenacious. That's not the same thing as clever."
—Tezzeret
The serum from the blinkmoths they gather greases the joints of witch engines.
A mirror to draw its eye, a rod to rouse its rage, and a sword to break its bonds.

"You are hopelessly obsolete, my brothers. Come and join the Great Work."
—Rhmir, Hand of the Augur

"Let their mindless armies come and face the might of genius."
—Varil, Neurok partisan
"Specimen 211 examination report. Observation: graft sublimation incomplete. Result: death. Prepare specimen 212."
"All plans begin as dreams. I intend to awaken them."
Phyrexians research with the grace of surgeons and the finesse of butchers.

"Under the suns, Mirrodin kneels and begs us for perfection."
—Geth, Lord of the Vault
At first, the Mirrans aimed for its exposed gut. The survivors quickly learned to do otherwise.
Having flesh is increasingly a liability on Mirrodin.

"Ours is a glorious transmission! Behold a future where all bow to the Father of Machines."
—Isila, Priest of Sheoldred
Even the dead are raw materials for the Phyrexian vision of perfection.

"The chest cavity is cleared of useless meat. I know just what to do with the space."
—Gyed, Vault Priest

"Perfection is at hand. You have been freed of weakness and made *compleat*."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One

"I believe many worlds will bow to Phyrexia. Mirrodin is merely the first."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One

"The union of the oil and necrogen has produced many pleasing reactions."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One
Life is ephemeral. Phyrexia is eternal.
Sadly, the extent of Gerkk's healing knowledge was "don't pick at it."
A productive warren requires a good deal of prodding.
Flame doesn't kneel to Phyrexia.
Shock one, awe the rest.
A golem's hands know no tenderness.
It chews open Mirrodin's husk and feeds on the outpouring of energy.
Mirran creatures that could withstand the Phyrexian oil found an abundance of crunchy snacks.

"A true warrior fights with whatever's handy."
—Qerk of the Secret Warren
Its flight sets the sky itself on fire.

"They believe they're driving us back, but we're leading them to their doom."
—Kethek, furnace stoker
Koth sent partisans into the Tangle to bring survivors to the safe haven of the tunnels below Kuldotha.
Being surrounded by goblins is less objectionable when they're fighting *for* you.

"All will be reforged in the fires of glory."
—Urabrask the Hidden
He didn't have a word for "home," but he knew it was something to be defended.

"Drive them back! Make their underworld into their grave!"
—Koth of the Hammer

"As long as we have the will to fight, we are never without weapons."
—Koth of the Hammer
"I never move the same way twice. Those rotters can't grasp chaos."

"We will reveal the futility of their heresy by showing them how fragile their relics are."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger

"The fangren fight without comfort of any kind. We can ask no less of ourselves."
—Tilien, Sylvok partisan

"So, the survivors from Oxid Ridge are on the move. Let them come and witness predation in its purest form."
—Glissa
As the green sun crowned, Phyrexian prophecies glowed on the Tree of Tales.
Her warriors are the last defense against the coming storm.
"Our land will not yield to Phyrexian corruption!"

"Even a nuisance such as the pistus fly has a purpose in our new world."
—Glissa
Phyrexia's spiral of consumption grows ever wider and darker.
As the Phyrexian contagion corroded Karn's body, the praetors whispered psalms to corrupt his mind.
Vorinclex removed its teeth so it wouldn't waste time chewing before moving to the next kill.
The fiercest hunters in the Tangle don't seek out the mantises. They *are* the mantises.
His crime was silence, and now he suffers it eternally.

"Domination by the strongest—that is all that matters in the Tangle now."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger
The Mirran partisans created hundreds of patrol sentinels to divert Phyrexian assaults from the Tangle.

"I admire it. Few pull off pluck and subservience at the same time."
—Ezuri, renegade leader

"We will fight as they do: our flesh protected behind metal."
—Tae Aquil, Viridian weaponsmith

"If there can be no victory, then I will fight forever."
—Koth of the Hammer
Mycosynth grew unfettered beneath the black lacuna, metastasizing into a matrix of noxious energy.

"Such a creation serves no purpose other than exterminating every one of us."
—Sadra Alic, Neurok strategist
Phyrexian smog clouds choked the skies, threatening creatures who couldn't comprehend the menace below.

"Use everything. Iron, rust, scrap . . . even the ground must join our cause."
—Ezuri, renegade leader

"Our glorious infection has taken hold."
—Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite

"Anything that watches without sleep and fights without fear is a valuable ally against the Phyrexians."
—Kara Vrist, Neurok agent
The faces of Geth's corpse-dredgers are disturbingly similar.
For the Phyrexians, death is not an end, nor a one-time occurrence.
Memnarch designed some myr to follow the levelers and reaffix lost parts. Mirran partisans put that instinct to good use.

"The Vanished must have sent it from beyond to aid us in this struggle."
—Kessla, Sylvok shaman

"Our cause will ripen in the fertile flesh of the unworthy."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One
Where nature impedes, Phyrexians overcome.
Basic senses like sight and taste are reserved for those in power.

"Pain isn't a negative stimulus. Pain is a sign of your imperfection."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One
Only the goblins could make a simple machine so complex.
They watch for a new master, one more sinister than the last.

"If that brain can't figure out the secret of the serum, then add more brains."
—Rhmir, Hand of the Augur
Adapted to tread on razorgrass, the rhino proved adept at treading on Phyrexians as well.

"It's a beautiful vision. Discarded debris is reborn as a singular entity."
—Urabrask the Hidden
It evades Phyrexians by hiding in the spaces between seconds.
It leaps from tree to tree, revealing the enemy's positions.
Partisan spies warned that no armor would protect the body from Phyrexian infection. Neurok strategists took that as a challenge.

"It will be battle-ready before our strike at Oxid Ridge, and it will guarantee our victory."
—Ketuc of the Helm

"A true Phyrexian predator. It will never know death, just as nature intended."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger

"Vulshok flail, Viridian shield, loxodon blade . . . Tazzir, bring the Moriok hook and assemble the rookies."
—Vy Covalt, Neurok agent
"Phyrexians can't corrupt what they can't get close enough to touch."

You will scream out your innermost secrets just to make it stop.

In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.

—Knight-Captain Wyhorn
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.

—Sorin Markov

"There is much to learn here, but few can endure the ringing of the spires."
—Nulakam the Archivist
Not every church is a place of faith.

"For centuries my creation kept this world in balance. Now only her shadow remains."
—Sorin Markov
Elves believe the hydra-god Progenitus sleeps beneath Naya, feeding on forgotten magics.

"It hurts more if you think about it."
—Hooks, Cabal torturer

—Kenzo the Hardhearted

—Azax-Azog, the Demon Thane

—Thor

—Doctor Strange

—Sif

—Magik, Illyana Rasputin

What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs in the afternoon, and three legs in the evening?
Few can withstand the wrath of the righteous.

"When one has witnessed the unspeakable, 'tis sometimes better to forget."

"May Svyelun and her tides favor you."

Through the pale door,

—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"

—Arna Kennerüd, skyknight

"Dwelling in icy mountain streams near goblin and orcish foes, the river merfolk were known for their stoicism."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. V*

"No one can catch what won't be caught."
—Kakra, sea troll
Fear the knight leaping from the water into the air, weapon ready.

"It was in Urza's journals that I finally found the secret at the core of the summonings."
—Journal, author unknown

"Beast. Defiler. The source of all my pain."

"Expect my visit when the darkness comes. The night I think is best for hiding all."

"Phyrexia's touch is painful to all but the blackest of hearts."
—Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen

"Those idiots should never have bred thrulls for combat!"

"Perhaps goblins are good for something after all."
—General Khurzog

"According to accepted theory, the grenade held some kind of flammable mixture and was carried to its target by a hapless goblin."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
If only it had three brains, too.

"While most overworlders fortunately don't realize this, gargoyles can be most delicious, providing you have the appropriate tools to carve them."
—Asmoranomardicadaistinaculdacar, The Underworld Cookbook

The Yeti's single greatest asset is its unnerving ability to blend in with its surroundings.

"Just the thing for those pesky water mages."

"Striking silent as a dream, Cutting short the strangled scream . . ."
—Tobrian, "Watchdragon"

"What tries to crush our spirit only strengthens our resolve."

—Ella Wheeler Wilcox, "Winds of Fate"

"We must shake her limbs and rattle her brains."

"Chub toad, chub toad
At the door.
Run away quick

—Traditional children's rhyme

"If the air must feed, let it take the self-righteous."

"Fyndhorn is our home."

"It's strange, but I can feel it when the land is corrupted. I understand why the Autumn Willow is so protective."

"That which nourishes can also bind."

"I hear there are bears—or spirits—that guard caravans passing through the forest."
—Gulsen, abbey matron
Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the basilisk's power.

"The danger in cultivating massive plants caught the elves by surprise."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. III*

"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!"
—William Shakespeare, King Lear

"When one wolf calls, others follow. Who wants to fight creatures that eat scorpions?"
—Maimun al-Wyluli, diary

"Few natural forces are as devastating as hunger."
—Kaysa, elder druid of the Juniper Order

". . . And at his passing, the bodies of the world's great warriors shall rise from their graves and follow him to battle."
—The Anvilonian Grimoire

"Centaurs will kill our aesthir if they can; they've always been enemies. Destroy the horse-people on sight."
—Arna Kennerüd, Skyknight

"My power is as vast as the plains, my strength is that of mountains. Each wave that crashes upon the shore thunders like blood in my veins."
—Dakkon Blackblade, Memoirs

"Relent, and you may transcend your situation."
—Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen

"There will come soft rains, and spring shall be amongst us, a welcome friend."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

Ashnod found few willing to trade their humanity for the power she offered them.
Ashnod invented several torture techniques that could make victims even miles away beg for mercy as if the End had come.

Valuing scholarship above all else, the inhabitants of the Ivory Tower reward those who sacrifice power for knowledge.
An early inspiration for Urza, Tocasia's onulets contained magical essences that could be cannibalized after they stopped functioning.

"Knowing its origins, how could they have thought they could control it?"
—Sorine Relicbane, Soldevi heretic
